info.title: gscandelari-ecommerce-api
info.description:
*[🇧🇷 Ler em português](/docs/)*

# Overview

A REST e-commerce API (Products, Orders, Payment, Cancellation/Refund) — portfolio project, running in real production. Microservices architecture: this document describes the public contract exposed by the **Orders** service, which holds every route a client of the API interacts with directly (`/produtos`, `/pedidos` — Portuguese names, kept as-is since they're the actual URL paths). A **Payments** service handles all Stripe integration (never called directly by you — see "Payment flow" below), and a **Notifications** service sends e-mail asynchronously when an order is confirmed or cancelled. All three sit behind a single public domain (Firebase Hosting as an API Gateway) — the URL you're using right now.

Full source code, architecture diagram and deploy walkthrough: [GitHub repository](https://github.com/GScandelari/gscandelari-ecommerce-api). Every business rule (RN01–RN33) with acceptance criteria: [`SPEC.md`](https://github.com/GScandelari/gscandelari-ecommerce-api/blob/main/SPEC.md) (in Portuguese).

# Authentication

Every endpoint below (except `GET /health`) requires a **Firebase ID Token** in the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. There's no API key — identity is always an authenticated Firebase Auth user (e-mail/password). Two things determine what you can do:

- **Being authenticated** (any valid user) is already enough to browse products and create/view/cancel your own orders.
- **Having the `admin: true` custom claim** on the token is required for product CRUD, freely changing an order's status, and processing refunds — the claim is the only source of authorization (never inferred any other way).

To try this documentation out via the **Authorize** button (top right): generate a real ID Token for a user of the `gscandelari-ecommerce-api` Firebase project via the [Identity Toolkit REST API](https://firebase.google.com/docs/reference/rest/auth#section-sign-in-email-password) (`accounts:signInWithPassword`) or the client SDK (`user.getIdToken()`), and paste the value (without the `Bearer` prefix) into the `bearerAuth` field. A token without the `admin` claim works normally for the non-administrative routes.

# Payment flow (Stripe, always test mode)

This project **never processes real money** — every key and Dashboard used is test/sandbox mode. `POST /pedidos` creates the order **and** a Stripe PaymentIntent in the same call (RN10/RN16), returning `paymentClientSecret` in the response — that's what a real UI would use with Stripe.js/Elements to collect the card. **Payment confirmation does not happen in this call**: it arrives asynchronously via a signed Stripe webhook (`payment_intent.succeeded`/`payment_intent.payment_failed`), received by the Payments service and relayed internally to Orders (RN12/RN13/RN17) — only then does `status` become `confirmado` and `paymentStatus` become `pago`. In other words: right after creating an order, `GET /pedidos/{id}` may still show `paymentStatus: "aguardando_pagamento"` until that webhook is processed — that's expected, not a bug.

To actually exercise payment, confirm the PaymentIntent (using `paymentClientSecret`) with a [Stripe test card](https://docs.stripe.com/testing#cards) (e.g. `4242 4242 4242 4242` for success).

# E-mail notification (Resend, best-effort)

When `status` transitions to `confirmado` or `cancelado`, the Notifications service sends an e-mail to the order's owner (Resend, always sandbox mode) — this happens asynchronously and is **best-effort**: a delivery failure never reverts or delays the response of any endpoint below.

# Out of scope for this document

`POST /webhooks/stripe` (received by Payments, called by Stripe — never by you) and the internal `/internal/*` routes of Orders/Payments (service-to-service communication, authenticated with a Google-signed ID token/OIDC, not Firebase Auth) exist and are real, but aren't part of this API's public contract — that's why they don't appear as endpoints below. Full details in the "Architecture" section of the [README](https://github.com/GScandelari/gscandelari-ecommerce-api#arquitetura).

servers.description: Same domain this documentation is hosted on — real production (API Gateway, Firebase Hosting) or the local Emulator Suite, depending on where /docs/en was accessed from.

tags.name: Orders
tags.description: Orders, payment, cancellation and refund (RN02-RN09, RN07a, RN10, RN16, RN28-RN33)

bearerAuth.description: Token obtained via Firebase Auth. Admin-only routes require the admin:true custom claim.

details.description: Present only for VALIDATION_ERROR originating from an invalid payload: the output of Zod's .flatten() (fieldErrors/formErrors).

precoUnitario.description: Unit price at the moment the order was created (frozen — future changes to the product's price never affect orders already created).

PedidoStatus.description: RN05: main flow pendente (pending) → confirmado (confirmed) → enviado (shipped) → entregue (delivered). Cancellation is reachable from pendente, confirmado or enviado — from enviado, it first becomes aguardando_devolucao (RN29), only then cancelado (RN30, Admin only). entregue and cancelado are terminal states. Values are kept in Portuguese — they're the literal strings the API returns.

PaymentStatus.description: RN10-RN15/RN31/RN32: independent of `status`. aguardando_pagamento (awaiting payment, initial) → pago (paid, on payment_intent.succeeded webhook) or falhou (failed, on payment_intent.payment_failed/canceled webhook — the order is also cancelled and stock restored). If an order with paymentStatus=pago is cancelled, it automatically becomes estorno_pendente (refund pending) — no call to Stripe happens at that moment. Only PATCH /pedidos/{id}/reembolsar (a manual Admin action) leads to reembolsado (refunded).

clienteId.description: Firebase Auth uid of the customer who owns the order.

paymentIntentId.description: Stripe PaymentIntent ID, created synchronously together with the order (RN16). Never null after a successful POST /pedidos.

paymentClientSecret.description: The PaymentIntent's client_secret — used by a real front-end with Stripe.js/Elements to collect the card and confirm payment. Never null after a successful POST /pedidos.

Unauthorized.description: Missing (`UNAUTHENTICATED`), invalid or expired authentication token.

Forbidden.description: Authenticated but not allowed to perform this action (`FORBIDDEN`) — missing the admin claim, or (on `/pedidos/{id}/cancelar`) the order belongs to a different customer.

ValidationError.description: Invalid payload or a business rule was violated (`VALIDATION_ERROR`).

PaymentGatewayError.description: Failed to communicate with the Payments service/Stripe (`PAYMENT_GATEWAY_ERROR`).

get.summary: Health check — the only endpoint without authentication

put.description: Admin only (RN01, RN07). Fully replaces the product — every field of `ProdutoInput` is required in the body, this is not a partial PATCH.

get.description: A customer sees only their own orders; an Admin sees all of them (RN08).

post.summary: Create an order and its Stripe PaymentIntent
post.description: Decrements the stock of every item transactionally (RN02, RN03, RN04) and, in the same call, creates a real Stripe PaymentIntent (test mode) via a synchronous internal call to the Payments service (RN10, RN16) — see "Payment flow" in the general description of this documentation. `status` starts as `pendente` and `paymentStatus` starts as `aguardando_pagamento`; confirmation arrives later, asynchronously, via webhook.

201.description: Order and PaymentIntent created; stock for the items already decremented.

400.description: Invalid payload, a product doesn't exist, or insufficient stock for some item (`VALIDATION_ERROR`, RN03).

502.description: Failed to create the PaymentIntent with Stripe (`PAYMENT_GATEWAY_ERROR`) — the order that was just created is automatically cancelled and stock restored (compensation).

patch.description: Admin only (RN05, RN07, RN07a). Accepts any structurally valid transition of the state machine (see `PedidoStatus`) — including advancing the normal flow (`pendente→confirmado→enviado→entregue`) and confirming a return (`aguardando_devolucao→cancelado`, RN30). If the transition is to `cancelado` from `pendente` or `aguardando_devolucao`, the items' stock is restored (RN07a/RN30); if the order had `paymentStatus: "pago"`, it automatically becomes `estorno_pendente` (RN31, no call to Stripe happens at this point — see `PATCH /pedidos/{id}/reembolsar`).

400.description: Structurally invalid status transition for the order's current state (`VALIDATION_ERROR`, RN05).

patch.summary: Owning customer cancels their own order
patch.description:
RN06, RN28, RN29 — behavior depends on the order's current `status`:
- `pendente` or `confirmado` → becomes `cancelado` directly; stock restored; if `paymentStatus` was `pago`, it automatically becomes `estorno_pendente` (RN31).
- `enviado` → becomes `aguardando_devolucao` (RN29) — the product is still physically with the customer; this transition does **not** restore stock nor change `paymentStatus`. Only an Admin can confirm the physical return afterwards (`PATCH /pedidos/{id}/status` to `cancelado`, RN30).
- Any other status (`entregue`, `aguardando_devolucao`, `cancelado`) → 400.

200.description: Order cancelled (or moved to aguardando_devolucao, if it was enviado).

400.description: Order is not in a status the Customer can cancel — only `pendente`, `confirmado` or `enviado` (`VALIDATION_ERROR`).

403.description: The order belongs to a different customer (`FORBIDDEN`).

patch.summary: Process a cancelled order's refund with Stripe
patch.description: Admin only (RN32) — a **manual, deliberate** action; no status transition ever triggers a refund automatically. Only allowed when `paymentStatus === "estorno_pendente"`. Calls `stripe.refunds.create` for the order's full total (no partial refunds) via the Payments service. Success → `paymentStatus: "reembolsado"` (the order's `status`, already `cancelado`, doesn't change). Failure calling Stripe → `paymentStatus` stays `estorno_pendente`, allowing a retry.

400.description: The order's paymentStatus is not estorno_pendente (`VALIDATION_ERROR`).
